summary:
After the tuna melt meltdown, Shane meets Rose Landry, has several deeply inconvenient revelations, and decides to do the only sensible thing: win Ilya back with sincerity, logistics, and a frankly alarming amount of emotional effort.
Ilya, meanwhile, mistakes every tender gesture for the kind prelude to an inevitable goodbye.
Or: Shane is living in a romcom. Ilya is living in a Russian tragedy.
bookmark_notes: Hello, the gentle cottage. Shane’s outstretched arms meeting Ilya the way Ilya deserves - pushing bravely past safety and what is known. Love isn’t always about meeting halfway - the line between two people is never quite so neat, but it sure isn’t just the work of one person standing on one side of the sand. This is love, and a plan, and Shane reaching out gently to bring his hands under Ilya’s heart, for him to say “it’s okay, you can rest now, I will hold it here for you for a little while”.
